subject: Demo insights + prioritized model plan (cost/latency/QA flags)
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Price <sara.price@finlytics.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-30T15:12:00Z
Subject: Thanks for the demo — quick recap & next steps

Hi Sara — thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

- Win criteria you reiterated: <25ms p95 for short queries, cost target <$0.002/token on average, and no regressions vs. current extractor on entity F1.
- Primary workload: mixed short Q&A (70%) + long-context summarization (30%).
- Data sensitivity: business data only; they will evaluate Private deployment for logs/retention.

Next steps I propose:
1) We run a focused benchmark across 3 candidate model profiles and send results + prompt set by next Wed (2027-07-06).
2) Security contacts will get the SOC2/arch docs — Monica, can you attach the short evidence pack?
3) Pricing/commit options — Ben to propose a committed throughput plan if benchmarks look good.

I've attached the recording and a starter prompt set (prompt_set_v2.txt). I'll follow up internally with the benchmark plan.

Thanks,
Dylan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
redwood.ai

Attachments: finlytics_demo_recording_20270630.mp4, prompt_set_v2.txt

From: Sara Price <sara.price@finlytics.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alan Reyes <alan.reyes@finlytics.com>, FinLytics Ops <ops@finlytics.com>
Date: 2027-06-30T17:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Thanks for the demo — quick recap & next steps

Thanks Dylan — that matches our notes. A couple clarifications:

- For the long-context use case we typically hit 8k tokens on input + 2k generated; latency target is less strict there, but quality matters (entity preservation).
- Security will run a short review; expect a questionnaire back by 2027-07-08.

Please flag any models that historically struggle with entity hallucination. We can share a few failing examples if helpful.

—Sara
Head of ML, FinLytics

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-07-01T09:30:00Z
Subject: Internal: benchmark plan & roles for FinLytics

Team — drafting our bench plan. Proposed candidate profiles (fast label):
A) rwd-compact-1 (FP16, 4-bit quant) — best cost, best latency for short queries, medium QA risk on long context.
B) rwd-balanced-2 (mixed precision) — mid cost, robust QA, slightly higher p95 latency.
C) open-xl-1 (open model opt) — lowest lic cost but variable inference characteristics on our runtime.

Plan: run 3 workloads across the provided prompt_set_v2.txt + 50 internal synthetic long-context docs. Metrics: p50/p95 latency, tokens/second cost estimate, entity F1 against labeled set, and hallucination rate (manual sample).
Ben — can you draft a committed throughput pricing slice if FinLytics wants Dedicated? Sean — run the profiling job and drop results in the Drive link below by 2027-07-06.

Monica
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: benchmarks_template.csv

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-07-06T14:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Internal: benchmark plan & roles for FinLytics

Upload complete — initial results are in the Drive folder (link below) and a short CSV attached. Top-level findings:
- rwd-compact-1: p95 = 24ms on short queries; cost est $0.0018/token; entity F1 = 0.81; some tokenization edge-cases caused split entities on long inputs.
- rwd-balanced-2: p95 = 48ms; cost est $0.0026/token; entity F1 = 0.89; stable on long-context.
- open-xl-1: p95 varied 60–120ms depending on batch; cost est $0.0012/token; entity F1 = 0.72 with higher hallucination rate.

Notes: we flagged 12 long-context examples where rwd-compact-1 dropped context; attached a short sample in the Drive. Recommend we present a prioritized shortlist to FinLytics (Compact => best MVP economics, Balanced => conservative production, Open-xl => cost-experiment with heavy QA).

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB_example_benchmark_drive_link
Attachments: benchmarks_20270706.csv

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Price <sara.price@finlytics.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-07-12T09:45:00Z
Subject: Model shortlist & recommendation — prioritized with tradeoffs

Sara — sharing our recommended shortlist and rationale after the focused benchmarks. TL;DR: two recommended options depending on FinLytics' priority.

1) MVP (Recommended first path): rwd-compact-1
- Rationale: Meets short-query p95 target (~24ms), cost meets your target (~$0.0018/token), and highest chance to hit go-live economics.
- Risk: Slight degradation on very long-context entity preservation; we mitigate with prefix-KV caching and a small context-trimming policy in the prompt set.
- Ask from you: accept pilot SLA with limited long-context SLA exemption for the first 6 weeks to tune prompts.

2) Conservative production (Recommended for strict QA): rwd-balanced-2
- Rationale: Stronger entity F1 (0.89) on our test set, fewer hallucinations in long documents; p95 ~48ms which is still acceptable for your summarization flows.
- Tradeoff: ~45% higher per-token cost vs. Compact.

3) Cost-experiment (Optional): open-xl-1
- Rationale: Lowest lic cost; we saw inconsistent p95 and higher hallucination. Could be viable behind heavy QA gates or if you only route non-sensitive or batch jobs there.

Attachments & links: demo recording (finlytics_demo_recording_20270630.mp4), benchmarks_20270706.csv, prompt_set_v2.txt, Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB_example_benchmark_drive_link

Next steps I propose:
- Let us know which path you prefer by 2027-07-19.
- If you pick Compact, Monica and Sean will run a 2-week prompt tuning cycle and we'll propose a Dedicated throughput slice (Ben).
- Security questionnaire answer will follow separately.

Happy to hop on a 30-min call to walk through the tradeoffs — what time next week works?

Thanks,
Dylan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
redwood.ai
